title: Prefetch Conductor: tenant-aware prefetch budget allocator and quant profile selector
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Introduces Prefetch Conductor service; tenant-level budgeted prefetching and quantization profile selection; new econ CLI dry-run and simulation mode; telemetry for prefetch hit/miss and budget burn-rate; safe fallbacks for cold-cache spikes.
description: Motivation: production workloads with bursty cold-start patterns were incurring unexpectedly high per-token cost due to aggressive cold-path allocations and suboptimal quant profile choices. This PR introduces a Prefetch Conductor — a tenant-aware agent that computes and applies short-lived prefetch budgets, coordinates KV/prefix warming, and selects a compatible quant/profile fallback when warm variants are unavailable. Key goals: reduce unit cost on cold bursts, keep 99th latency within SLO, and provide safe fallbacks that avoid quality regressions. Summary of changes: 1) new service: services/prefetch_conductor — budget allocator, admission control, and decision-graph for fallback quant selection; 2) econ CLI: redwood-cli econ prefetch --dry-run/--simulate to evaluate tenant policies against sampled traces; 3) telemetry: metrics (prefetch_budget_assigned, prefetch_budget_used, prefetch_hit_ratio, quant_fallbacks, prefetch_evictions) and tracing tags to tie budgets to tenant and route; 4) runtime hooks: lightweight prefill API changes to accept budget tokens and target quant profile hints; 5) policy config: introduce econ.prefill.policies v1 schema, documented in docs/econ/prefetch.md; 6) test harness: perf/fixtures/prefetch_simulator with synthetic burst traces and integration tests that assert unit-econ improvements and stable latencies. Commits (high level): - Add Prefetch Conductor scaffolding and decision graph (asha/prefetch/initial) - Implement budget allocator and telemetry hooks (asha/prefetch/budgeting) - Add econ CLI simulation mode and dry-run reporting (asha/cli/prefetch-sim) - Wire runtime prefill API and safe-fallback paths (asha/runtime/prefill-hook) - Add unit + integration tests and docs (asha/tests/docs) Files changed (high level): services/prefetch_conductor/* (new service and controller), redwood-cli/econ_prefetch.py (new commands), runtime/prefill_api.py (hook and minimal schema change), config/schemas/econ_prefill_v1.yaml (policy schema), telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml (new metrics), perf/fixtures/prefetch_simulator/* (test traces and runner), docs/econ/prefetch.md, tests/integration/test_prefetch_budget.py, charts/helm/prefetch-conductor-values.yaml. Checklist: - [x] Service design and decision-graph documented - [x] Backwards-compatible runtime hook with safe defaults - [x] CLI dry-run and simulation implemented - [x] Unit and integration tests added - [x] Telemetry added and dashboards referenced in docs - [x] Feature flagged off by default for gradual rollout Review conversation summary: Liam: "Overall clean design. Two asks: add tenant-id tags to budget metrics and make eviction logs structured for tracing." Asha: "Added tenant tags and switched eviction logs to structured JSON in telemetry commit; updated docs." Priya: "Please add an integration test that simulates a 5-minute cold spike and assert budget burn-rate < 25% of expected and 99th latency within 1.2x baseline." Asha: "Added prefiller integration scenario and assertions; included synthetic traces in perf/fixtures." Marco: "Concern about potential race between budget assignment and concurrent prefill tasks; request to add a small optimistic lock and a metrics counter for contention." Asha: "Added lightweight optimistic seqnum check and prefetch_contention counter; explained rationale inline and added comment linking to decision-graph." CI: initial run showed a flaky integration test (tests/integration/test_prefill_budget.py::test_cold_spike_simulation) failing on the first attempt due to timing sensitivity; re-ran CI after increasing timeouts and switching to deterministic seed; all checks passed on rerun. Security review: no new privileged surface; prefill agent runs with same RBAC as existing batch orchestrator and honors tenant isolation. Performance note: local perf harness shows ~18-26% token-cost reduction for synthetic bursty traces with minimal impact to average latency; joint evaluation on staging showed 12% cost reduction for a mid-sized tenant during a synthetic cold-start campaign. Rollout plan: feature flagged default-off, gradual enable for opt-in tenants via Console and API; initial rollout to internal tenants and two pilot customers next sprint. Merge: squashed merge performed by Priya Desai on 2026-02-21 after final approvals. Related: references design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/briefs/ENG-1792-prefetch-conductor and Linear tasks ENG-1792, ENG-1823. Notes for operators: use redwood-cli econ prefetch --simulate --tenant <id> to preview expected budget allocation; dashboards updated at Observability -> Econ -> Prefetch. If rollback needed: set feature flag to off and scale service to zero via helm chart.
